# Topaz DEX

## There’s more to crypto than waiting.

Trade across 5 networks, earn from liquidity and voting, or let Topaz Auto manage a concentrated position for you.

The homepage includes a working swap. [Start trading](https://www.topazdex.com/swap) or explore the earning paths below.

## Find your way to earn.

- **Earn trading fees**: Provide liquidity to earn trading fees while your position stays unstaked. [Explore fee earning](https://www.topazdex.com/explore/pools?earning=fees).
- **Earn token rewards**: Stake eligible liquidity for TOPAZ or xTOPAZ rewards, depending on network. [Explore emissions](https://www.topazdex.com/explore/pools?earning=emissions).
- **Put your votes to work**: Vote for pools to earn a share of allocated trading fees and incentives. [Explore voting](https://www.topazdex.com/vote).

Unstaked liquidity earns trading fees; gauge-staked liquidity earns emissions. These APRs are separate returns. Concentrated positions earn only while in range.

Earning links retain the existing pool filters and initialize the relevant APR sort. Explicit sort choices persist in the URL. APRs vary and do not guarantee a return.

## Find your next move.

Browse up to three fresh, curated pools on the selected network, ordered by reported TVL with a $100 minimum. Market examples use chain-qualified data from https://api.topazdex.com/v1. Browsing does not switch a wallet. [All pools](https://www.topazdex.com/explore/pools).

## Different chains. One Topaz.

Topaz is live on BNB Chain (56), Robinhood Chain (4663), Base (8453), Ethereum (1) and Arc (5042). BNB is the hub for xTOPAZ entry and redemption; xTOPAZ bridging and local voting connect the five networks. Arc trades USDC directly, with no wrapped native. Each network has its own markets and voting. xTOPAZ represents shares backed by permanently locked TOPAZ on BNB. Bridge and stake it on supported networks to vote locally. Its conversion rate is not fixed at 1:1; redemption creates a permanent veTOPAZ lock on BNB.

## Topaz in motion.

Homepage TVL and rolling 24-hour volume combine the multichain API’s independently observed networks. Cumulative volume retains the existing historical series. Live values and their independent timestamps appear on the page; this Markdown does not pin them. [Data and methodology](https://www.topazdex.com/stats/methodology).

## You’ve built the token. Give it a market.

[Create a pool](https://www.topazdex.com/positions/create) or [add voting incentives](https://www.topazdex.com/incentivize). These are separate actions.

## Confidence starts with clarity.

Shieldify · 25 April 2026: A published review of dynamic swap fees and selected changes to Topaz’s core and Slipstream contracts on BNB Chain. The report covers its specified code revisions. It does not establish coverage of all current deployments, the omnichain release or every interface feature.

[Published Shieldify report](https://github.com/shieldify-security/audits-portfolio/blob/main/reports/Topaz-Dex-Security-Review.pdf) · [Contracts](https://www.topazdex.com/docs/contracts) · [Source](https://github.com/topazdex).

## Community and resources

- [X](https://x.com/TopazDex): updates and announcements.
- [Telegram](https://t.me/TopazDex): questions and community conversation.
- [Docs](https://www.topazdex.com/docs)
- [Protocol analytics](https://www.topazdex.com/stats)
- [Agent index](https://www.topazdex.com/llms.txt)
- [Skill](https://www.topazdex.com/skill.md)

# Contracts

Topaz is live on BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Base, Ethereum and Arc. This address book lists the deployed hub, spoke and interface contracts by network. The original BNB core sections retain their links; complete network tables follow. Verify the network and contract role before using an address.

## Multichain deployment status

**Updated September 15, 2026.** Topaz DEX, xTOPAZ bridging and voting are live on BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Base, Ethereum and Arc. xTOPAZ entry and redemption use the BNB vault. Each table below identifies its network; identical addresses on different networks are separate deployments.

The hub extension includes XTopaz, VeTopazVault, WrapRouter, a system-gauge strategy, EpochCoordinator and XTopazOFTAdapter. Each spoke has its own DEX contracts, XTopazOFT, XTopazVotingVault, SpokeEmissionReceiver and composers. [Multichain contract groups](https://www.topazdex.com/docs/developers/multichain).

Each network table includes its DEX, token, bridge, voting and interface infrastructure. Contract-only composers and the xTOPAZ zap are identified separately from the actions exposed in the app. Per-pool and gauge instances are available through chain-qualified Explore and API records. [Networks and availability](https://www.topazdex.com/docs/multichain).

selectedFunctions.label: Topaz addLiquidity
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Only the direct V2 Router deployments on BNB Chain, Base and Ethereum are admitted. Each is a constructor-configured Router, not an upgradeable proxy; retained full source has no delegate fallback. Explorer heuristic proxy banner on the spoke pages is not a resolved implementation. Factories/registry, tokens and gauge dependencies remain external; their full independent runtime/safety attestation is not asserted.

Amounts are raw token base units and LP-token units, not USD or normalized decimals. selectedFunctions.label: Topaz addLiquidity
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Only the direct V2 Router deployments on BNB Chain, Base and Ethereum are admitted. Each is a constructor-configured Router, not an upgradeable proxy; retained full source has no delegate fallback. Explorer heuristic proxy banner on the spoke pages is not a resolved implementation. Factories/registry, tokens and gauge dependencies remain external; their full independent runtime/safety attestation is not asserted.

Amounts are raw token base units and LP-token units, not USD or normalized decimals. ETH-named methods use the chain native gas token (BNB on chain 56, ETH on 1/8453) and the constructor wrapped-native address. Nonpayable methods require zero native value; payable exact-native swaps use msg.value, addLiquidityETH refunds unused native to the caller.

Caller-funded swaps pull the effective sender input, or wrap native input, and execute fixed pool.swap calls with empty callback data. Route factory must be registry-approved; zero factory selects default. Routes must form a coherent available path; recipient is caller-selected. Ordinary methods enforce deadline and output or liquidity-leg minima; fees, reserve rounding, token taxes and market changes affect outcomes.

Liquidity add may create a default-factory pool, pulls only chosen caller amounts and mints LP to the specified recipient. Router quotes subtract MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY=1000 units for initial LP estimates and use proportional integer math thereafter; actual LP issuance/burn is delegated to the chosen pool. Removal pulls caller LP, burns it and directs assets to the recipient; fee-on-transfer removal checks pool-reported amounts, not a guarantee of net received tokens.

Fee-on-transfer swaps use reserve/balance deltas. Token-to-native fee-on-transfer swaps and fee-on-transfer removal can use the router entire residual token balance; no ownership of preexisting dust or guaranteed net recipient amount is promised.

V2 zapIn/zapOut are fixed swap-plus-liquidity operations, not opaque executors. They have leg minima but no deadline parameter. zapIn splits caller input, optionally stakes minted LP into the Voter-selected gauge for recipient; its internal gauge allowance does not grant wallet authority. Dust refunds sweep full router balances to effective sender. zapOut pulls raw msg.sender LP and refunds the resulting chosen asset to effective sender. Direct canonical wallet calls only; no trusted-forwarder or signing grant is added.

Concentrated-liquidity, UniversalRouter/Permit2, CL/Auto zaps with external executable payloads, bridge/voting infrastructure and unsupported Robinhood/Arc networks are not admitted by this finite V2 inventory. UNSAFE swap is excluded because caller supplies unchecked intermediate amounts without an output minimum.

selectedFunctions.label: Topaz addLiquidity
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Only the direct V2 Router deployments on BNB Chain, Base and Ethereum are admitted. Each is a constructor-configured Router, not an upgradeable proxy; retained full source has no delegate fallback. Explorer heuristic proxy banner on the spoke pages is not a resolved implementation. Factories/registry, tokens and gauge dependencies remain external; their full independent runtime/safety attestation is not asserted.

Amounts are raw token base units and LP-token units, not USD or normalized decimals. ETH-named methods use the chain native gas token (BNB on chain 56, ETH on 1/8453) and the constructor wrapped-native address. Nonpayable methods require zero native value; payable exact-native swaps use msg.value, addLiquidityETH refunds unused native to the caller.

Caller-funded swaps pull the effective sender input, or wrap native input, and execute fixed pool.swap calls with empty callback data. Route factory must be registry-approved; zero factory selects default. Routes must form a coherent available path; recipient is caller-selected. Ordinary methods enforce deadline and output or liquidity-leg minima; fees, reserve rounding, token taxes and market changes affect outcomes.

Liquidity add may create a default-factory pool, pulls only chosen caller amounts and mints LP to the specified recipient. Router quotes subtract MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY=1000 units for initial LP estimates and use proportional integer math thereafter; actual LP issuance/burn is delegated to the chosen pool. Removal pulls caller LP, burns it and directs assets to the recipient; fee-on-transfer removal checks pool-reported amounts, not a guarantee of net received tokens.

Fee-on-transfer swaps use reserve/balance deltas. Token-to-native fee-on-transfer swaps and fee-on-transfer removal can use the router entire residual token balance; no ownership of preexisting dust or guaranteed net recipient amount is promised.

V2 zapIn/zapOut are fixed swap-plus-liquidity operations, not opaque executors. They have leg minima but no deadline parameter. zapIn splits caller input, optionally stakes minted LP into the Voter-selected gauge for recipient; its internal gauge allowance does not grant wallet authority. Dust refunds sweep full router balances to effective sender. zapOut pulls raw msg.sender LP and refunds the resulting chosen asset to effective sender. Direct canonical wallet calls only; no trusted-forwarder or signing grant is added.

Concentrated-liquidity, UniversalRouter/Permit2, CL/Auto zaps with external executable payloads, bridge/voting infrastructure and unsupported Robinhood/Arc networks are not admitted by this finite V2 inventory. UNSAFE swap is excluded because caller supplies unchecked intermediate amounts without an output minimum.

selectedFunctions.label: Topaz addLiquidity
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Only the direct V2 Router deployments on BNB Chain, Base and Ethereum are admitted. Each is a constructor-configured Router, not an upgradeable proxy; retained full source has no delegate fallback. Explorer heuristic proxy banner on the spoke pages is not a resolved implementation. Factories/registry, tokens and gauge dependencies remain external; their full independent runtime/safety attestation is not asserted.

Amounts are raw token base units and LP-token units, not USD or normalized decimals. ETH-named methods use the chain native gas token (BNB on chain 56, ETH on 1/8453) and the constructor wrapped-native address. Nonpayable methods require zero native value; payable exact-native swaps use msg.value, addLiquidityETH refunds unused native to the caller.

Caller-funded swaps pull the effective sender input, or wrap native input, and execute fixed pool.swap calls with empty callback data. Route factory must be registry-approved; zero factory selects default. Routes must form a coherent available path; recipient is caller-selected. Ordinary methods enforce deadline and output or liquidity-leg minima; fees, reserve rounding, token taxes and market changes affect outcomes.

Liquidity add may create a default-factory pool, pulls only chosen caller amounts and mints LP to the specified recipient. Router quotes subtract MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY=1000 units for initial LP estimates and use proportional integer math thereafter; actual LP issuance/burn is delegated to the chosen pool. Removal pulls caller LP, burns it and directs assets to the recipient; fee-on-transfer removal checks pool-reported amounts, not a guarantee of net received tokens.

Fee-on-transfer swaps use reserve/balance deltas. Token-to-native fee-on-transfer swaps and fee-on-transfer removal can use the router entire residual token balance; no ownership of preexisting dust or guaranteed net recipient amount is promised.

V2 zapIn/zapOut are fixed swap-plus-liquidity operations, not opaque executors. They have leg minima but no deadline parameter. zapIn splits caller input, optionally stakes minted LP into the Voter-selected gauge for recipient; its internal gauge allowance does not grant wallet authority. Dust refunds sweep full router balances to effective sender. zapOut pulls raw msg.sender LP and refunds the resulting chosen asset to effective sender. Direct canonical wallet calls only; no trusted-forwarder or signing grant is added.

Concentrated-liquidity, UniversalRouter/Permit2, CL/Auto zaps with external executable payloads, bridge/voting infrastructure and unsupported Robinhood/Arc networks are not admitted by this finite V2 inventory. UNSAFE swap is excluded because caller supplies unchecked intermediate amounts without an output minimum.

Only the direct V2 Router deployments on BNB Chain, Base and Ethereum are admitted. Each is a constructor-configured Router, not an upgradeable proxy; retained full source has no delegate fallback. Explorer heuristic proxy banner on the spoke pages is not a resolved implementation. Factories/registry, tokens and gauge dependencies remain external; their full independent runtime/safety attestation is not asserted.

Amounts are raw token base units and LP-token units, not USD or normalized decimals. ETH-named methods use the chain native gas token (BNB on chain 56, ETH on 1/8453) and the constructor wrapped-native address. Nonpayable methods require zero native value; payable exact-native swaps use msg.value, addLiquidityETH refunds unused native to the caller.

Caller-funded swaps pull the effective sender input, or wrap native input, and execute fixed pool.swap calls with empty callback data. Route factory must be registry-approved; zero factory selects default. Routes must form a coherent available path; recipient is caller-selected. Ordinary methods enforce deadline and output or liquidity-leg minima; fees, reserve rounding, token taxes and market changes affect outcomes.

Liquidity add may create a default-factory pool, pulls only chosen caller amounts and mints LP to the specified recipient. Router quotes subtract MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY=1000 units for initial LP estimates and use proportional integer math thereafter; actual LP issuance/burn is delegated to the chosen pool. Removal pulls caller LP, burns it and directs assets to the recipient; fee-on-transfer removal checks pool-reported amounts, not a guarantee of net received tokens.

Fee-on-transfer swaps use reserve/balance deltas. Token-to-native fee-on-transfer swaps and fee-on-transfer removal can use the router entire residual token balance; no ownership of preexisting dust or guaranteed net recipient amount is promised.

V2 zapIn/zapOut are fixed swap-plus-liquidity operations, not opaque executors. They have leg minima but no deadline parameter. zapIn splits caller input, optionally stakes minted LP into the Voter-selected gauge for recipient; its internal gauge allowance does not grant wallet authority. Dust refunds sweep full router balances to effective sender. zapOut pulls raw msg.sender LP and refunds the resulting chosen asset to effective sender. Direct canonical wallet calls only; no trusted-forwarder or signing grant is added.

Concentrated-liquidity, UniversalRouter/Permit2, CL/Auto zaps with external executable payloads, bridge/voting infrastructure and unsupported Robinhood/Arc networks are not admitted by this finite V2 inventory. UNSAFE swap is excluded because caller supplies unchecked intermediate amounts without an output minimum.
